title: Success is a System: Designing Better Done Screens
summary: This reel outlines five key decisions for designing effective success states that keep users engaged rather than hitting a dead end. It covers the importance of specificity, providing next actions, matching dismissal to stakes, creating open loops, and using celebration sparingly.

transcript.text: Success is a system. Three done screens. Only one keeps the user.
Say what happened. Success tells you nothing. Invoice sent to Northwind Labs, due October 12th.
Specifics are the proof it worked. A vague success feels like a maybe.
Every success screen offers the next action. Send an invoice? View it or send another.
A checkmark with no button is a dead end. The user closes the tab right there.
Dismissal follows stakes. A saved setting gets a toast that leaves in four seconds.
A payment gets a page that stays, with a receipt and an email. Nobody screenshots a toast.
Success is not the end. Leave one open loop. Track the payment, share the report, invite the team.
A finished task with a thread to pull brings people back.
Celebration scales with rarity. Confetti on every save trains people to ignore it.
Save it for the first invoice paid. Rare joy lands. Constant joy is noise.
Five decisions. One success state that keeps the user moving.
Now make Claude Code think like a senior UX designer. UX Engine designs the screen before coding, audits what is broken, reviews the diff, and kills the AI look. Link in bio.

on_screen_text: Think like a senior UX designer.
design_principles: Always provide a next step to avoid dead ends
Dismissal duration based on stakes (Toast vs. Page)
before_after: Transformation from a generic 'Success!' checkmark with a single 'OK' button to a detailed, actionable success page with specific data and retention loops.
